mainTopic: The four fasts of זכריה, why תשעה באב is stricter, who identifies the fasts and how, and whether מגילת תענית was cancelled
overview: This amud begins in the middle of a discussion about why messengers are not sent out to announce the months of תמוז and טבת, even though they contain fast days. רבי שמעון חסידא notes that a פסוק in זכריה calls the same four days both 'fast' and 'joy'. רב פפא explains that there are three situations: with peace they are joyful, with persecution they are fasts, and in between, fasting is optional. That is why no messengers are needed for those months. תשעה באב is an exception and is always required, because many disasters happened on it. A ברייתא then brings רבי עקיבא's identification of the four fasts, which follows the order of the months. רבי שמעון disagrees about the tenth-month fast and identifies it so that the list also follows the order of the tragedies. Next, אמוראים argue whether מגילת תענית, the list of joyous days on which fasting is forbidden, was cancelled after the חורבן. Challenges from חנוכה and from the 3rd of תשרי are answered: חנוכה stays because its miracle is publicized, and new days were added only while the בית המקדש stood.

steps.title: The verse calls the same days both fasts and days of joy
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר ביזנא quotes רבי שמעון חסידא, who points out a puzzle in a פסוק from זכריה. The verse names four fast days and then says they will be days of joy.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב חנא בר ביזנא said in the name of רבי שמעון חסידא: What does the verse mean, 'Thus says ה' of hosts: The fast of the fourth month, the fast of the fifth, the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth will become joy and gladness for the house of Judah'? The verse calls them 'fast' and also calls them 'joy and gladness'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a teaching to answer the earlier question of why no messengers go out for תמוז and טבת. The teaching opens by pointing out that one verse describes the same days in two opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse first says 'the fast of' these months and then says they 'will be' joy. These sound like two opposite statuses for the same days. The puzzle sets up a resolution that will tell us when these days are fasts and when they are not.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (an opening formula for explaining a verse)

steps.confusionAlert: 'The fourth', 'the fifth', and so on mean the fourth and fifth MONTHS, counting from ניסן. They are not days of the week. The fourth month is תמוז, the fifth is אב, the seventh is תשרי (צום גדליה), and the tenth is טבת.

phrases.english: As Rav Ḥana bar Bizna said
phrases.notes: The opening 'ד' (as) shows this answers the previous question about messengers.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon Ḥasida said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Thus said the Lord of hosts:
The fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the fifth,
and the fast of the seventh, and the fast of the tenth,
shall become joy and gladness for the house of Judah."
It calls them "fast,"
and it calls them "joy and gladness"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question earlier about why messengers are not sent for תמוז and טבת.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can the same days be called both fasts and days of joy?

steps.title: Peace makes them days of joy, and no peace makes them fasts
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון חסידא resolves the puzzle. When there is peace, the days are joyful. When there is no peace, they are fasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: When there is peace, they will be days of joy and gladness. When there is no peace, they are fasts.
steps.whatsHappening: The puzzle is answered by saying the status of these days depends on the situation of the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two descriptions in the verse are not a contradiction. They describe two different times. This answer still seems to make the fasts required whenever there is no peace. That leaves the messenger question open, which is why רב פפא will refine it next.

keyTerms.meaning: At a time when there is peace

phrases.english: At a time when there is peace —
they will be for joy and gladness;
when there is no peace — a fast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The status depends on the times. With peace, the days are joyful. Without peace, they are fasts.

steps.title: A middle situation where fasting is optional
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that there are really three situations. With peace, the days are joyful. With persecution (שמד), they are fasts. With neither, fasting is up to the people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: This is what it means. When there is peace, they will be days of joy and gladness. When there is persecution, they are fasts. When there is no persecution and also no peace, if people want they fast, and if they want they do not fast.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא refines the previous answer by adding a middle category. This finally explains why no messengers are sent for תמוז and טבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer had only two options: peace or a required fast. רב פפא adds a middle state, which is no persecution but also no full peace. In that state the fasts are voluntary. Something voluntary does not need a messenger to announce the exact date.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying (a reinterpretation formula)
Persecution, harsh decrees against the Jewish people

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the idea that the minor fasts depend on communal acceptance. They are not automatically required in every period.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁלוֹם — יִהְיוּ לְשָׂשׂוֹן וּלְשִׂמְחָה,
phrases.english: At a time when there is peace — they will be for joy and gladness;
when there is persecution — a fast;
when there is no persecution and no peace —
if they wish they fast, if they wish they do not fast.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines step 2 by adding a third, optional category.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Whenever there is no peace, the fasts would be required, so messengers should be needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a time with no persecution and no peace, fasting is optional, so messengers are not needed.

steps.title: Then תשעה באב should also be optional
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא. If these fasts are optional, תשעה באב should be optional too. Yet the משנה says messengers go out for אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, תשעה באב should also be like this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב פפא's rule by applying it to תשעה באב, the fast of the fifth month in the same verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תשעה באב is listed in the same verse as the other three fasts. If they are optional in the middle situation, so is it. Then why does the משנה require messengers for the month of אב?

phrases.english: If so, the Ninth of Av also?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that the fasts of the verse are optional in the middle situation
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: תשעה באב is in the same verse, so it should be optional too. That contradicts the משנה, which sends messengers for אב.

steps.title: תשעה באב is different because of its many disasters
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that תשעה באב is different because many tragedies happened on it. So its fast stays required.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: תשעה באב is different, since troubles multiplied on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא defends his rule by explaining that תשעה באב is an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תשעה באב is still one of the fasts of the verse. But because so many disasters piled up on that one day, it is not optional like the others. It is required even in the middle situation, so messengers are sent for it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שָׁאנֵי תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב,
phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: The Ninth of Av is different,
since calamities were multiplied on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: תשעה באב should be optional like the other fasts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because so many disasters happened on it, תשעה באב remains required.

steps.title: The list of disasters on תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רב פפא by quoting a known teaching. On תשעה באב both Temples were destroyed, ביתר was captured, and ירושלים was plowed over.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the master said: On תשעה באב the Temple was destroyed, both the first time and the second time. ביתר was captured, and the city was plowed over.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show that troubles really did multiply on תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This list is the evidence behind רב פפא's claim in step 5. Four major disasters fell on one date. That makes it far more severe than the other fasts.

keyTerms.meaning: As the master said (quoting a known teaching)
ביתר, the last stronghold of the בר כוכבא revolt

steps.whatToRemember: The minor fasts can depend on the times, but תשעה באב is always required because of its many disasters. That is why messengers go out for אב.

phrases.english: As the Master said: On the Ninth of Av
the Temple was destroyed, the first time and the second,
and Beitar was captured, and the city was plowed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 5.
steps.raayaObject: That troubles multiplied on תשעה באב
steps.raayaSupportSource: A known teaching quoted as 'דאמר מר', listing four disasters on that date

steps.title: רבי שמעון disagrees with four of רבי עקיבא's explanations
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי שמעון, who says there are four verses that רבי עקיבא explained in a way he does not. This sets up the dispute over the four fasts.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי שמעון said, there are four things that רבי עקיבא would explain, and I do not explain them the way he does.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא opens a new topic, which is how to identify the four fasts of זכריה. It does this by introducing a disagreement between רבי עקיבא and רבי שמעון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled yet. The line simply announces that רבי עקיבא's readings will be presented and that רבי שמעון disagrees. The first reading, about the fasts in זכריה, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Like him, the way he does

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi Shimon said:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעָה דְּבָרִים הָיָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דּוֹרֵשׁ,
phrases.english: Four things Rabbi Akiva would expound,
and I do not expound them as he does:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new line of discussion about identifying the fasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון disagrees with רבי עקיבא's explanation of four verses.

steps.title: The fast of the fourth is the ninth of תמוז
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says 'the fast of the fourth' is the ninth of תמוז, when the walls of ירושלים were breached. He proves it from a verse in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The fast of the fourth' is the ninth of תמוז, when the city was breached. As it says: 'In the fourth month, on the ninth of the month, the famine grew strong in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land, and the city was breached.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is רבי עקיבא's first explanation. He identifies the date of the fast of the fourth month and backs it up with a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא links the fast to the actual event, the breaching of the city walls. The verse in ירמיהו gives the exact date as the ninth of the fourth month.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introducing a verse as proof)

steps.confusionAlert: Today we fast on the 17th of תמוז, not the 9th. The ninth was when the walls were breached at the time of the First Temple. The 17th was the breach at the time of the Second Temple. Do not mix up the two dates.

phrases.english: "The fast of the fourth" — this is the ninth of Tammuz,
on which the city was breached,
as it is stated: "In the fourth month, on the ninth of the month,
the famine was severe in the city,
and there was no bread for the people of the land,
and the city was breached."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first of רבי עקיבא's four explanations announced in step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fast of the fourth is the ninth of תמוז, the day the city was breached.

steps.title: Why it is called the fourth: the fourth of the months
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks why the fast is called 'fourth'. The answer is that תמוז is the fourth month counting from ניסן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why is it called 'fourth'? Because it is the fourth of the months.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא clarifies the name 'fourth' with a quick question and answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number in the verse refers to the order of the months. Months are counted from ניסן, so תמוז is the fourth. This sets the pattern for naming the other fasts by their month number.

keyTerms.meaning: Fourth of the months (counting from ניסן)

phrases.english: And why does it call it "fourth"? —
The fourth of the months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the term 'fourth' used in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תמוז is the fourth month counting from ניסן.

steps.title: The fast of the fifth month is תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains that 'the fast of the fifth' is תשעה באב, the day the בית המקדש was burned. It is called 'fifth' because אב is the fifth month.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The fast of the fifth' is the ninth of אב, when the House of our God was burned. Why is it called 'fifth'? Because אב is the fifth of the months.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא moves on to the second fast in the verse and tells us which day it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as the fast of the fourth. First he names the day and the tragedy, then he explains the number. The number counts months from ניסן, so אב is the fifth.

keyTerms.meaning: The fast of the fifth month
The House of our God, the בית המקדש
Of the months, counting from ניסן

phrases.english: 'The fast of the fifth': this is the ninth of Av,
on which the House of our God was burned.
And why does he call it 'fifth'?
Because it is the fifth of the months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבי עקיבא's list after the fast of the fourth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fast of the fifth is תשעה באב, the day of the burning of the בית המקדש.

steps.title: The fast of the seventh month is the fast of גדליה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains that 'the fast of the seventh' is the third of תשרי, when גדליה בן אחיקם was killed by ישמעאל בן נתניה. This teaches that the death of צדיקים is as serious as the burning of the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The fast of the seventh' is the third of תשרי, when גדליה בן אחיקם was killed. Who killed him? ישמעאל בן נתניה killed him. This teaches you that the death of the righteous is equal to the burning of the House of our God. Why is it called 'seventh'? Because תשרי is the seventh of the months.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא identifies the third fast and adds a lesson about why a fast was made for one man's death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fast does not remember a disaster to the city or the בית המקדש. It remembers the murder of one righteous leader. Because חז״ל made a fast for it just like for the burning of the בית המקדש, we learn that the death of צדיקים is just as tragic.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jewish governor left in ארץ ישראל after the destruction
Is equal to, weighs the same as

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the famous idea that the death of צדיקים is like the burning of the בית המקדש. It also explains why צום גדליה is part of the yearly fasts.

phrases.english: 'The fast of the seventh': this is the third of Tishrei,
on which Gedaliah son of Ahikam was killed.
And who killed him?
Ishmael son of Nethaniah killed him,
to teach you that the death of the righteous is equal
to the burning of the House of our God.
And why does he call it 'seventh'?
Because it is the seventh of the months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in רבי עקיבא's list of fasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fast of the seventh is ג׳ תשרי, for the killing of גדליה. The death of צדיקים equals the burning of the בית המקדש.

steps.title: The fast of the tenth month is עשרה בטבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains that 'the fast of the tenth' is the tenth of טבת, when the king of בבל began the siege of ירושלים. He proves it from a verse in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The fast of the tenth' is the tenth of טבת, when the king of בבל laid siege to ירושלים. As the verse says: 'The word of ה׳ came to me in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth of the month: Son of man, write down the name of this day. The king of בבל has laid siege to ירושלים on this very day.' Why is it called 'tenth'? Because טבת is the tenth of the months.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא identifies the last fast in the verse and brings a פסוק to show the siege began on that date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof works because the verse in יחזקאל gives the exact date, the tenth day of the tenth month, and says the siege began then. So the fast of the tenth month marks the start of the siege.

keyTerms.meaning: Laid siege to, closed in on

phrases.english: 'The fast of the tenth': this is the tenth of Tevet,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבּוֹ סָמַךְ מֶלֶךְ בָּבֶל עַל יְרוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.english: on which the king of Babylonia laid siege to Jerusalem,
as it says: 'And the word of the Lord came to me
in the ninth year, in the tenth month,
on the tenth of the month, saying:

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן אָדָם כְּתׇב לְךָ אֶת שֵׁם הַיּוֹם
phrases.english: Son of man, write down for yourself the name of the day,
of this very day:
the king of Babylonia has laid siege to Jerusalem.'
And why does he call it 'tenth'?
Because it is the tenth of the months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי עקיבא's list with the fourth and final fast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fast of the tenth is עשרה בטבת, when the siege of ירושלים began.

steps.title: Why is the siege fast listed last?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: the siege happened first, so shouldn't the verse have listed this fast first?
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it fitting to write this one first?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא himself raises a problem with his own reading. If the tenth-month fast marks the start of the siege, it should come first in the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The siege was the first event in the whole story of the destruction. Yet the verse lists it last. The question is why the verse does not follow the order in which things happened.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that... (opens a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא הָיָה רָאוּי זֶה לִכְתּוֹב רִאשׁוֹן?
phrases.english: But wasn't it fitting to write this one first?

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא הָיָה רָאוּי זֶה לִכְתּוֹב רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the order of the verse according to רבי עקיבא's reading in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the verse under רבי עקיבא's own reading. He raises this question himself, about the siege fast being listed last.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first event should be listed first, but the verse lists it last.

steps.title: The verse follows the order of the months
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the verse lists the fasts by the order of the months in the year, not by the order the events happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: So why was it written here? To list the months in their proper order.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא answers his own question. The verse is arranged by calendar order: fourth, fifth, seventh, tenth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is not telling the story in order. It lists the fasts by month, starting from ניסן. טבת is the tenth month, so its fast comes last even though the siege came first.

phrases.english: And why was it written here?
In order to arrange the months in their proper order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the organizing principle of the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse should list events in the order they happened.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse lists the fasts in calendar order, by month.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the tenth-month fast is חמשה בטבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees. He says the fast of the tenth is the fifth of טבת, the day the news reached the exiles in בבל that ירושלים had been destroyed. They made the day of the news like the day of the burning.
steps.simpleTranslation: But I do not say this. Rather, 'the fast of the tenth' is the fifth of טבת, when the news reached the exile that the city had been struck. As the verse says: 'In the twelfth year of our exile, in the tenth month, on the fifth of the month, a survivor from ירושלים came to me saying: The city has been struck.' They made the day of the news like the day of the burning.
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי שמעון gives his own reading of the tenth-month fast, which is different from רבי עקיבא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree the fast is in טבת, but they disagree about which day and which event. For רבי שמעון it is the day the exiles heard the bad news, which came after the destruction. He proves the date from a different verse in יחזקאל.

keyTerms.meaning: But I do not say so (opens a disagreement)
The exile, the Jews in בבל

steps.confusionAlert: רבי שמעון also places this fast in טבת, the tenth month. The disagreement is about which day in טבת and which event, not about the month.

phrases.english: But I do not say so. Rather:
'The fast of the tenth': this is the fifth of Tevet,
on which the report came to the exile
that the city had been struck,
as it says: 'And it was in the twelfth year,
in the tenth month, on the fifth of the month, of our exile,
the survivor from Jerusalem came to me
saying: The city has been struck.'
And they made the day of the report like the day of the burning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי שמעון rejects רבי עקיבא's reading of the tenth-month fast from step 12 and offers his own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fast of the tenth is ה׳ טבת, the day the news of the destruction reached the exiles.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: my reading keeps the events in order
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון argues his reading is better. In his view the verse lists the fasts both by month and by the order the tragedies happened. In רבי עקיבא's view the first event is listed last.
steps.simpleTranslation: My words seem better than his. I say the first-listed is the first event and the last-listed is the last event. He says the first-listed is the last event and the last-listed is the first event. He counts only by the order of the months, while I count by the order of the tragedies as well.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives a reason his reading is better than רבי עקיבא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the siege happened first but is listed last, so the verse is out of story order. For רבי שמעון, the news fast in טבת came after everything else, so listing it last fits both the calendar and the story. A reading that matches on both counts is more convincing.

keyTerms.meaning: My words seem more correct than his

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: the tenth-month fast is עשרה בטבת (the siege), and the verse follows only the order of the months. רבי שמעון: it is חמשה בטבת (the news), and the verse follows both the order of the months and the order of the tragedies.

phrases.english: And my words seem better than his words,
for I say about the first that it was first
and about the last that it was last,
while he says about the first that it was last
and about the last that it was first.
Only that he counts by the order of the months,
while I count by the order of the tragedies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי שמעון supports his reading from step 15 by comparing it with רבי עקיבא's answer in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבי שמעון's reading of the fast of the tenth as ה׳ טבת
steps.raayaSupportSource: The order of the verse: his reading keeps the list in the order the events happened, while רבי עקיבא's puts the first event last.

steps.title: A dispute: Has the list of joyous days been cancelled?
steps.stepSummary: רב and רבי חנינא say מגילת תענית is cancelled. רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי say it is not cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב and רבי חנינא say: מגילת תענית has been cancelled. רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי say: מגילת תענית has not been cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents a new מחלוקת between אמוראים about whether the special happy days listed in מגילת תענית are still kept today. It is setting up the explanation of each side, which comes in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מגילת תענית is an old list of days when good things happened to the Jewish people, so fasting and eulogies are forbidden on them. The question is whether these days were cancelled once the בית המקדש was destroyed and we went into exile.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated (introduces a dispute between אמוראים)
An ancient list of joyous days on which fasting and eulogizing are forbidden
Has been cancelled / is no longer in force

steps.confusionAlert: Despite the name, מגילת תענית ('Scroll of Fasting') is NOT a list of fast days. It is a list of happy days on which you may NOT fast.

phrases.english: It was stated: Rav and Rabbi Chanina say:
Megillat Ta'anit has been cancelled.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:
Megillat Ta'anit has not been cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the identity of the four fast days in the פסוק to a related question: are the joyous days of מגילת תענית still kept?
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two positions: מגילת תענית is cancelled (רב, רבי חנינא) versus not cancelled (רבי יוחנן, רבי יהושע בן לוי).

steps.title: Why רב and רבי חנינא say the list is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק makes the four fasts into happy days only when there is peace. Without peace they are fasts. The days of מגילת תענית follow the same rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and רבי חנינא say מגילת תענית is cancelled. This is what the פסוק means: when there is peace, these days will be for joy and gladness. When there is no peace, they are fasts. And those days of מגילת תענית are just like these fast days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning of רב and רבי חנינא. They read the פסוק as linking joy to times of peace.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the four fasts will become days of joy. רב and רבי חנינא understand that joy depends on there being peace, meaning the בית המקדש is standing. They apply the same rule to the happy days of מגילת תענית: without peace, those celebrations stop too, so the list is cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what [the פסוק] is saying
Peace (here: times when the בית המקדש stands and there is no oppression)
For joy and gladness (words from the פסוק in זכריה)
And those are also like these: the מגילת תענית days are like the fasts

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the pointing words. Here הָנֵי ('these') means the four fasts from the פסוק, and הָנָךְ ('those') means the days of מגילת תענית.

phrases.english: Rav and Rabbi Chanina say
Megillat Ta'anit has been cancelled,
this is what [the verse] is saying:
phrases.notes: Refers to the פסוק in זכריה about the four fasts.

phrases.english: at a time when there is peace —
they will be for joy and gladness;
when there is no peace — a fast.
And those [days of Megillat Ta'anit] are also like these [fasts].
phrases.notes: Their joy also depends on peace, so without peace they are cancelled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first opinion stated in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Joy on special days depends on peace. With no peace, the days of מגילת תענית are cancelled, just as the four days go back to being fasts.

steps.title: Why רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי say the list still stands
steps.stepSummary: Only the four fasts were tied by the תורה to the בית המקדש. The days of מגילת תענית stay as they always were.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and רבי יהושע בן לוי say מגילת תענית is not cancelled. It is only these four fasts that the Merciful One made depend on the building of the בית המקדש. But those days of מגילת תענית stay exactly as they were.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the other side: the condition in the פסוק applies only to the four fasts, not to the days of מגילת תענית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This side agrees that the פסוק ties the four fasts to the בית המקדש. But they say you cannot extend that condition to other days. The happy days of מגילת תענית were never made conditional, so they remain in force even in exile.

keyTerms.meaning: That He made them depend on
The Merciful One (a name for ה׳, referring to the Torah or the נביא)
The building of the בית המקדש
They stand as they stood: they remain in force

steps.confusionAlert: The pointing words mean the same thing here as in the previous step. הָנֵי ('these') means the four fasts from the פסוק, and הָנָךְ ('those') means the days of מגילת תענית.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole מחלוקת is about one question: does the 'peace' condition in the פסוק apply only to the four fasts (רבי יוחנן, רבי יהושע בן לוי), or also to the days of מגילת תענית (רב, רבי חנינא)?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי אָמְרִי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi say:
Megillat Ta'anit has not been cancelled —
it is these [fasts] that the Merciful One made dependent
on the building of the Temple,
but those [days of Megillat Ta'anit] — remain as they were.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי הוּא דִּתְלִינְהוּ רַחֲמָנָא בְּבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the second opinion in step 17 and limits the reading given in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the four fasts depend on the בית המקדש. The days of מגילת תענית remain in force.

steps.title: רב כהנא challenges from a fast on חנוכה in לוד
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells that a fast was declared on חנוכה in לוד. רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע showed they rejected it and told the people to fast again to atone for fasting. This suggests the days of מגילת תענית still apply.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא objected: There was a story where they declared a fast on חנוכה in לוד. רבי אליעזר went down and bathed, and רבי יהושע cut his hair. And they said to them: Go and fast to make up for the fact that you fasted.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא brings a ברייתא to attack רב and רבי חנינא, who said מגילת תענית is cancelled. The next step gives רב יוסף's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חנוכה is one of the days listed in מגילת תענית, and this story took place after the חורבן. If the list were cancelled, fasting on חנוכה should have been fine. Yet the חכמים treated the fast as a mistake that itself needed atonement, which shows the list was still in force.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection (usually from a ברייתא or משנה)
He bathed (forbidden on a fast, so it showed he rejected the fast)
He cut his hair (also a sign of rejecting the fast)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Go and fast for what you fasted' does not mean the fast was good. It means the fast was wrong, and they needed another fast as תשובה for having fasted on a forbidden day.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana raised an objection:
There was an incident, and they decreed a fast on Chanukah in Lod,
and Rabbi Eliezer went down and bathed,
and Rabbi Yehoshua [went down] and cut his hair.
And they said to them:
phrases.notes: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע said this to the people who had fasted.

phrases.english: Go out and fast for [the sin of] what you have fasted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the opinion explained in step 18 (רב and רבי חנינא).
steps.kashyaTarget: רב and רבי חנינא's claim that מגילת תענית has been cancelled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: חנוכה is a day listed in מגילת תענית. After the חורבן, the חכמים still treated fasting on it as forbidden, so the list cannot have been cancelled.

steps.title: רב יוסף: חנוכה is different because it has a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers the challenge from לוד. חנוכה is a special exception because it comes with a מצוה (lighting candles). So it was not cancelled together with the rest of מגילת תענית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: חנוכה is different, because it has a מצוה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends the view that מגילת תענית is cancelled. He says the story from לוד proves nothing about the other days, because חנוכה is a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge said that if fasting on חנוכה was forbidden, then all of מגילת תענית must still be in force. רב יוסף answers that חנוכה has its own מצוה of lighting candles, which the other days do not have. So חנוכה could survive even if the rest of the list was cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: A commandment; here, lighting the חנוכה candles

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Chanukah is different, since there is a מצוה (of lighting candles).
phrases.notes: This sets חנוכה apart from the other days in מגילת תענית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the לוד story in step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the proof to an exceptional case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a fast on חנוכה was rejected, it seemed that all of מגילת תענית was still in force.
steps.terutzMaskana: חנוכה is an exception because of its מצוה, so the proof does not carry over to the other days.

steps.title: אביי: then cancel the מצוה too
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects רב יוסף's reason. If the festival were cancelled, its מצוה could simply be cancelled along with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Let the festival be cancelled, and let its מצוה be cancelled with it!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף. Having a מצוה is no reason to keep a festival alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of candles exists only because the festival exists. If the Sages cancelled the festival, the מצוה would fall away with it. So the מצוה cannot be the thing that protects חנוכה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, student and colleague of רב יוסף

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Let it (the festival) be cancelled, and let its מצוה be cancelled!
phrases.notes: The מצוה depends on the festival, so it cannot protect the festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the answer given in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב יוסף's first reason only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The מצוה is part of the festival, so whatever cancels the festival would cancel the מצוה too.

steps.title: רב יוסף: חנוכה is different because its miracle is publicized
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives a new reason. The miracle of חנוכה is widely known among all of Israel, so it would not be right to cancel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: חנוכה is different, because its miracle is publicized.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף drops his first answer and gives a better one. חנוכה survives because its miracle is famous and accepted by everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא tells us the first answer has been dropped. The new reason does not depend on the festival itself. It rests on a fact in the world: the miracle is known and celebrated by all of Israel. So the 'cancelled' view stands, and חנוכה is the exception.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (dropping the earlier answer for a new one)
The miracle is publicized and widely known

steps.whatToRemember: According to the view that מגילת תענית was cancelled, חנוכה remains because its miracle is publicized, not simply because it has a מצוה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why חנוכה (like פורים) is still kept today, while almost all the other days of מגילת תענית are not.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said:
Chanukah is different, because its miracle is publicized.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, שָׁאנֵי חֲנוּכָּה דְּמִיפַּרְסַם נִיסָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that אביי rejected in step 22.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מצוה was what kept חנוכה, but אביי showed that does not work.
steps.terutzMaskana: חנוכה remains because its miracle is publicized, so the לוד story does not prove that the rest of מגילת תענית is in force.

steps.title: רב אחא בר הונא quotes the 3rd of תשרי entry
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר הונא begins a new challenge. He quotes מגילת תענית about the 3rd of תשרי. The Greeks forbade mentioning God's name. After the חשמונאים won, they required God's name even in legal documents.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר הונא raised an objection: On the 3rd of תשרי the mention (of God's name) was removed from documents. The Greek kingdom had decreed that Jews may not mention the name of Heaven. When the חשמונאים grew strong and defeated them, they ruled that people should mention the name of Heaven even in documents. They would write: 'In year such-and-such of יוחנן the כהן גדול of God Most High.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge against the view that מגילת תענית was cancelled. First it tells the story behind one of the days on the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מותיב tells us a challenge is coming. This part is only the background. To show loyalty to God after the Greek decree, the חשמונאים had God's name written even in everyday legal papers. The actual challenge comes two steps later.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection (from a source)
Legal documents, such as loan papers

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Huna raised an objection:
On the third of Tishrei
the mention (of God's name) was removed from documents.
phrases.notes: This is the line quoted from מגילת תענית itself.

phrases.english: For the Greek kingdom had issued a decree

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא לְהַזְכִּיר שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם עַל פִּיהֶם,
phrases.english: not to mention the name of Heaven on their lips,
and when the Hasmonean kingdom grew strong and defeated them,

phrases.aramaic: הִתְקִינוּ שֶׁיְּהוּ מַזְכִּירִין שֵׁם שָׁמַיִם אֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁטָרוֹת.
phrases.english: they enacted that people should mention the name of Heaven even in documents.
And this is how they would write:

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁנַת כָּךְ וְכָךְ לְיוֹחָנָן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
phrases.english: 'In year such-and-such of Yochanan the High Priest
of God Most High.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to the view that מגילת תענית is cancelled, now that the חנוכה proof has been answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רב and רבי חנינא that מגילת תענית is cancelled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: it tells the history of the 3rd of תשרי festival. The attack itself comes in step 26.

steps.title: The Sages cancel the practice and make the day a festival
steps.stepSummary: The Sages worried that a paid-off loan document with God's name on it would be thrown into the garbage. So they stopped the practice and made that day a festival.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the Sages heard about this, they said: Tomorrow this borrower will pay his debt, and the document will end up thrown on a garbage heap. So they cancelled the practice, and they made that day a festival.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues quoting the source. It explains why the Sages stopped writing God's name in documents and turned that day into a festival.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a loan is paid, the document is useless and gets thrown away, which would disgrace God's name. The Sages stopped the practice and marked the day it ended as a festival. The key point for the challenge: this festival day was set up long after earlier days on the list.

keyTerms.meaning: A festival day (here, a day on which fasting is forbidden)

phrases.english: And when the Sages heard of the matter, they said:
Tomorrow this one will pay his debt,
and the document will be found thrown on a garbage heap,
phrases.notes: God's name would then be disgraced.

phrases.english: so they cancelled them (the mentions of God's name in documents),
and that day they made into a festival.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes quoting the source that step 24 began.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Sages cancelled the writing of God's name in documents and made the 3rd of תשרי a festival.

steps.title: Why add new days if the old ones were cancelled?
steps.stepSummary: The challenge is stated. If מגילת תענית was cancelled, it makes no sense that the Sages kept adding new festival days to it. That suggests the list stays in force.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think מגילת תענית was cancelled, would they cancel the first days and add new ones?!
steps.whatsHappening: Now רב אחא בר הונא gives the actual challenge, based on the story. Adding new days to the list shows it was not meant to be cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 3rd of תשרי was added to the list later than the earlier days. It would make no sense to cancel the earlier days while new ones were still being added. So מגילת תענית seems to be still in force, against רב and רבי חנינא.
steps.confusionAlert: The challenge is not about whether we write God's name in documents. It is about the fact that a new festival day was added to מגילת תענית, which suggests the list was meant to last.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בָּטְלָה מְגִילַּת תַּעֲנִית —
phrases.english: And if you would think that Megillat Ta'anit was cancelled —
would the first ones be cancelled,
while later ones are added?!
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question: it makes no sense.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ בָּטְלָה מְגִילַּת תַּעֲנִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the story from steps 24-25 to make the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of רב and רבי חנינא that מגילת תענית is cancelled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Sages kept adding new festival days to the list. That shows the list was meant to stay in force, which goes against the claim that it was cancelled.

steps.title: The new festival was added while the Temple still stood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the 3rd of תשרי was added to מגילת תענית while the בית המקדש was standing. At that time the list was fully in force. That says nothing about what happened after the חורבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? A time when the בית המקדש was standing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 26. It explains that the Sages added the new festival day back when the בית המקדש still stood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that adding new days shows the list is always in force. The answer splits time into two periods: while the בית המקדש stood, and after it was destroyed. New days were added in the first period, when everyone agrees מגילת תענית applied. The opinion that it was cancelled refers only to the time after the חורבן, so there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: "What case are we dealing with here?" A standard phrase that answers a question by narrowing the case to a specific situation.

steps.whatToRemember: מגילת תענית was fully in force while the בית המקדש stood, and new days could be added to it then. The claim that it was cancelled refers only to the time after the חורבן.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think this answer means the 3rd of תשרי festival was never real. It was real and fully binding. The answer only limits *when* it was binding: while the בית המקדש stood.
steps.whyThisMatters: This time split is the key to the whole discussion. Everything about whether the fasts and festivals of מגילת תענית still apply depends on telling apart the period of the בית המקדש from the period after its destruction.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
phrases.notes: A standard opening that narrows a source to a specific situation in order to answer a challenge.

phrases.english: At a time when the Temple was standing.
phrases.notes: Before the חורבן, every day listed in מגילת תענית was in force, so new days could be added.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers רב אחא בר הונא's challenge in step 26 by limiting the added festival to the period of the בית המקדש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific time period (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the Sages kept adding festival days to מגילת תענית, the list seemed to stay in force forever, which would contradict the view that it was cancelled.
steps.terutzMaskana: The days were added while the בית המקדש stood, when the list was in force by everyone's view. The cancellation applies only after the חורבן.
